_comment: Curated mappings from a Helix career to a National Careers Service job
profile, for cases the title matcher cannot decide on its own.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The matcher accepts only an exact normalised title
match. 737 public NCS profiles exist and only 54 matched that way, so most
careers fall back to a derived estimate. Every entry here promotes one career
from a derived estimate to career-specific evidence on the next run.
THE TEST APPLIED TO EACH ENTRY. Not 'are these titles similar' but 'is the
range this profile publishes an honest answer for this career'. A qualifier
that only names a sector or setting (healthcare, clinical, scientific) is
usually safe: a marketing manager in healthcare is a marketing manager. A
qualifier that marks a different profession, a different registration or a
materially different pay market is not, however similar the words look.
HOW TO ADD ONE. docs/MARKET-DATA-AUDIT.md lists the current candidates with
the profile each nearly matched. Key = the career title as
title_matcher.normalise() produces it; value = the slug from
https://nationalcareers.service.gov.uk/job-profiles/<slug>. Check a key with:
python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); \
from market_data.title_matcher import normalise; \
print(normalise('Andrology Scientist'))"
WHAT NOT TO ADD. Never alias a seniority variant to its base profile.
'Senior Biomedical Scientist' is not the same job as 'Biomedical scientist',
and mapping it would publish an entry-grade range as career-specific fact
about a senior post. The matcher rejects these deliberately and the audit does
not list them. Adding one by hand defeats the check.
Never add an alias to make coverage look better. A transparent derived
estimate is better than a confident wrong one, and doing nothing is always a
safe choice. Removing an alias is equally safe: the career simply returns to a
derived estimate.
DO NOT LOWER THE MATCHER'S 0.6 CANDIDATE THRESHOLD to surface more of these.
That is the obvious next idea and it is a bad one. The band just below it was
examined: 178 careers, and they are dominated by false friends. 59 of them hit
'Clinical scientist', 13 hit 'Nurse', 8 hit 'Surgeon' and 3 hit 'Pathologist'
purely because they end in the same word — so 'CAR-T Scientist' would be
offered the salary of a protected NHS profession, and 'Veterinary Surgeon' the
salary of a medical consultant. 'Workforce Development Manager' matches
'Business development manager' on two shared tokens and is a different job.
The threshold is doing exactly what it should. The five sub-discipline entries
below were taken from that band by direct inspection, on the narrow ground that
the target profile's own text explicitly covers the application area.
AFTER EDITING:
python tools/market_data/enrich.py --all
python tools/market_data/validate.py --previous <the file before>

_note: Candidates looked at and deliberately left as derived estimates, so the
same ten are not re-litigated at every review. Each names the reason.
Nothing here is read by the pipeline.

clinical geneticist.reason: A clinical geneticist is a medical consultant on the medical pay scale. The geneticist profile publishes 35k-58k for a laboratory science role; this career currently derives 40k-145k, which is the right shape. The alias would cut the top of the range by nearly two thirds and label the result career-specific fact.

clinical biochemist.reason: Clinical biochemistry is a healthcare science specialism entered as a Clinical Scientist, with HCPC registration and Agenda for Change pay. The biochemist profile describes research and industry roles at 28k-53k and understates it.

clinical photographer.reason: Clinical photography is a healthcare science role in medical illustration. The photographer profile's 17k-45k is dominated by commercial and freelance work with a quite different pay structure.

health psychologist -> clinical psycholo.reason: Rejected as a SIBLING, then accepted against the GENERIC occupation instead. Health psychologist and clinical psychologist are two different HCPC-protected professions with different training routes, and registration as one is not a licence to practise as the other. But a health psychologist is unambiguously a psychologist, so the alias now points at the general 'psychologist' profile. The distinction is the rule: a named specialism may map to its parent occupation, never sideways to a sibling specialism.

analytical chemist, synthetic chemist an.reason: Accepted on the titles, then withdrawn on the evidence. The chemist profile publishes 26k-40k, and these were the only direct anchors in Pharma, Biotech R&D & Manufacturing — so derivation spread that range across 44 further careers, including Antibody Scientist, Biologics Scientist and Cell Line Development Scientist, which are PhD-level industry posts paying well above it. The validator flagged 46 careers sharing one range and it was right. Two careers gained a career-specific label and 44 were made materially less accurate. An alias in a family with few anchors carries far more weight than the one career it names, so the low end of a generic profile can poison a whole family.

cell biologist / molecular biologist and.reason: Rejected because derivation already does better. These careers derive from the NCS research scientist profile at 27k-48k, which fits a PhD-level research post; the general biologist profile publishes 24k-40k and would lower them while adding a career-specific label. An alias is only an improvement if it beats what derivation already produces.

gcp auditor and the other GxP auditors.reason: The auditor profile describes inspecting financial records and procedures. A GxP auditor audits pharmaceutical quality systems against regulatory standards. Same word, different occupation.

genetic counsellor.reason: A genetic counsellor is a registered healthcare science professional working in clinical genetics, not a talking-therapies counsellor. The 25k-48k counsellor range does not describe the role.

plant pathologist and veterinary patholo.reason: The pathologist profile at 54k-115k describes a medical pathologist working in hospitals and laboratories — a doctor. Chemical pathologist is one and was accepted; plant and veterinary pathology are different disciplines entirely and were not.

medical writer and the other medical wri.reason: The writer profile publishes no salary at all, so there is nothing to gain, and medical writing is in any case a distinct and better-paid niche from general authorship.

clinical dental technician.reason: A clinical dental technician holds a separate GDC registration and can treat patients directly; a dental technician works in a laboratory and does not. Different scope, different registration, different pay.

clinical pharmacologist.reason: The title covers both a medical specialty and a non-medical pharma role, with very different pay. Genuinely ambiguous, so it stays derived.

health economist.reason: Health economics and outcomes research is a distinct and better-paid niche in pharma and consultancy. The economist profile's 28k-60k describes government and financial economists and would understate it.

pharmaceutical sales representative.reason: Pharmaceutical sales pay is structurally different from general sales — higher base plus a commission structure. The 23k-50k general range would understate it while claiming to be career-specific.

healthcare business intelligence analyst.reason: Business intelligence analysis and business analysis are different jobs: one builds reporting and data models, the other elicits requirements and improves processes. The word overlap is coincidental.

public health intelligence analyst.reason: The profile displays as 'Intelligence analyst' but is the criminal intelligence analyst profile — policing and national security. Nothing to do with public health surveillance. A false friend created by dropping 'health' as a setting word.
